extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) Benchmark
extraction.description: The Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) benchmark is a multimodal dataset designed to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in recognizing conflicting commands. It comprises 20,000 conflicts evenly distributed between language-language (L-L) and vision-language (V-L) paradigms, with 4 tasks in each paradigm. L-L tasks include RuleConflict, AttributeConflict, ExclusionConflict, and ForbbidenConflict. V-L tasks include OCRConflict, FigureConflict, GeometricConflict, and SemanticConflict. The benchmark was constructed using a novel automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang
extraction.publisher: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Fudan University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
extraction.citeAs: Gao, J., Gan, L., Li, Y., Ye, Y., Wang, D. (2024). Dissecting Dissonance: Benchmarking Large Multimodal Models Against Self-Contradictory Instructions. arXiv:2408.01091v2.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created using AutoCreate, a novel automatic dataset creation framework that leverages programs and large language models. AutoCreate starts from several task-relevant seeds and maintains a seed pool. During each cycle, AutoCreate includes two branches—language and vision—each consisting of a generator, decorator, and cleaner. The cleaner excludes data that does not meet standards, and data is fed back into the seed pool after quality check by human experts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Others (Automatic LLM-based dataset generation)
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset was generated from scratch using LLMs starting from manually input task-relevant seeds. For SemanticConflict, images are sourced from the ImageNet dataset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For V-L conflicts, image captions are modified to introduce conflicts. For FigureConflict, numerical data is manipulated by changing the maximum value to the minimum value. For GeometricConflict, phrases describing objects are modified to refer to non-existent objects. For SemanticConflict, correct labels in questions are substituted with similar but different objects.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each branch of AutoCreate consists of a generator (creates initial language/vision data), a decorator (creates self-contradictions in the generated data), and a cleaner (removes data that does not meet quality standards). Human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset contains self-contradictory instructions generated automatically by LLMs following structured prompts for each of the 8 conflict tasks. Human experts rigorously checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset. Three levels of splits (SCI-Core 1%, SCI-Base 10%, SCI-All 100%) were manually provided according to the occurring frequency of conflict types.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Evaluation of LMM replies is conducted by both human experts and LLM agents (e.g., GPT-4). Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate were calculated between LLM agents and human expert evaluations, showing close alignment (e.g., GPT-4V: Spearman's ρ=0.881, 94% concordance).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large Language Models (LLMs) including GPT-4, ChatGPT, ChatGLM are used as generators, decorators, cleaners, and evaluation agents in the AutoCreate framework.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies. The AutoCreate framework facilitates creation of diverse instruction datasets, promoting inclusivity in AI research. The CaP approach integrates external cognition into multimodal models, enhancing context-aware understanding. By improving dissonance detection, the approach boosts LMM performance and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms; more modalities could be included. No fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree. The paper does not provide a detailed study on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating (testing/benchmarking) Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) regarding their capability to detect self-contradictory instructions in both language-language and vision-language paradigms.
